# Module hierarchy

<!-- Generated by Verilog/tests/gen_hierarchy.py from a real elaboration by yosys 0.66+183 (hierarchy -top). Do not edit by hand - run python3 tests/gen_module_docs.py from Verilog/ (in WSL) to regenerate the module docs, MODULES.md and this page. -->

What sits inside what, for every build top. Each top was elaborated with the file list, defines and include folders its own build uses, so `ifdef`s, generate blocks and parameters are already applied. Every module links to its page; the full list is in [MODULES.md](MODULES.md).

How to read the trees:

- Click a module with a triangle to fold its contents in or out. The top two levels start open.
- `name` after a module is the instance name in its parent.
- A module that one parent uses several times goes on one line: `x16` and the instance names. What is inside it is drawn once, under that line.
- A sub-tree is drawn in full the first time it appears on this page. Later copies that are exactly the same (same modules, same instance names, all the way down) say "same as above" and link to it, also across boards.
- "vendor" marks a part that is not ours and is not followed: FPGA primitives, PLLs, vendor IP, and the MiSTer and MEGA65 frameworks. For MiSTer and MEGA65 the tree starts at our top below the framework.
- ROM/RAM init files do not change which instances exist, so yosys was given empty stand-ins for them.

## Simulation (Verilator)

Build: `Verilog/runSim/Makefile`, default settings (`make compile`: USE_LATCHES=0, VERILOG_TAPE=1, SD_STORAGE=1, CACHE=1).

Defines: `VERILATOR_SIM`, `FPGA_FF_MODE`, `ND_SDRAM_PACK16`, `ND120_VERILOG_DEVICES`, `ND120_SD_STORAGE`, `ND120_SD_CARD_IMG="../SD-FAT/sim/nd_boot_card.img"`.

The simulation models in `SD-FAT/sim/` are behavioural test models yosys cannot elaborate ($random, file I/O); they contain no module instances and were read as black boxes (their own port list, empty body).

261 of our modules, 2906 module instances, 13 levels deep. Vendor parts: none.

## MiSTer

Build: `Verilog/fpga/mister/nd120.qsf` (which sources `files.qip`). The Quartus top is the framework's `sys_top`; the tree starts at the core's `emu` below it.

Defines: `FPGA_FF_MODE=1`, `BOARD_CLK_FREQ=20000000`, `UART_BAUD_RATE=115200`, `ND120_UART_DELAY_FRAMES=173`, `MAIN_RAM_SDRAM=1`, `ND_SDRAM_PACK16=1`, `ND_SDRAM_DQ16=1`, `ND_SDRAM_REFRESH_US=7`, `QUARTUS_RAM_INFER=1`, `ND120_PANEL_CLOCK=1`, `ND120_MIPS_TAP=1`, `ND120_NO_CACHE=1`, `SKIP_WCS_LOAD=1`, `QUARTUS_LATCH_RENAME=1`.

`build_id.v` is written by the build just before synthesis; a stand-in with the same kind of content was used.

The SystemVerilog top was read by the yosys slang plugin (yosys' own reader cannot pass the unpacked arrays in it to `hps_io`). The modules it instantiates were given to slang as black boxes made from their own headers, then replaced by the real files, which yosys elaborated as for every other top. Framework and vendor parts stay black boxes.

Not followed (framework): 3 file(s).

277 of our modules, 2877 module instances, 13 levels deep. Vendor parts: `altera_pll`.
